newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents per lb lower on Friday, although traders said market sentiment was relatively bullish after Thursday's firm close.
"It may dip early because everyone went home long and then shoot back up," said one trader.
New York arabica futures ended higher in choppy dealings on Thursday, boosted by commission house and light trade buying late in the day.

September arabicas rose 4.30 cents per lb on the day, to 179.85, after ranging from 181.00 to 168.75. Spot July, which enters delivery period today, finished 5.85 cents higher, at 195.90, while the outer months closed up 4.20 to 6.00.
The July/September switch widened to 16.05 cents at the close, from 14.50 cents on Wednesday.
On the charts, traders pegged September resistance at 184.50, while near-term support was seen at 175.00, then 168.00.
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 39 bags as of June 18, to 47,325 bags. There were 2,250 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, no damaging cold is indicated over the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, although there may be some disruptions to the harvest from scattered showers, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday.
In London, robusta futures were firmer early Friday, but off highs in quiet, switch-dominated trading. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was up $16, to $1,876, after peaking at $1,895.
